text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers.

- Finance Minister Viktor Klima extends deadline for Austro-Italian consortium bid for government's stake in Creditanstalt-Bankverein until Friday, threatens to start talks with other potential bidders if deadline is not met.
- Chancellor Franz Vranitzky promises 300 million schillings in aid for Palestinians after talks with Yassir Arafat in Gaza.
- Germany's Vereinigte Aluminium Werke are said to top the list of bidders for Austrian aluminum maker Amag, to be sold by state-holding OeIAG.
- Austrian railways OeBB and its partners, the country's utilities, aim to become Austria's number-two telecommunications provider.
- Far-right leader Joerg Haider nominates university sports lecturer Franz Linser to top the Freedom Party's ticket for European Parliament elections on October 13.
- Austria's ailing tourism industry is weighed down by high VAT rates, study says.
- New orders in Austria's battered construction industry have continued to drop in the third quarter, hit lowest level since the start of the 1990s.
- Oberbank says first half operating profit rose 18 percent to 339 million schillings, but warns earnings growth will slow in the second half.
- Austrian high-tech companies begin to feel the pinch amid increasing cut-backs in European space programmes.
- Tyrolean Airways, majority-owned by Austrian Airlines, to invest 800 million schillings in new aircraft before the end of the year.
